item.title: Aid might cut $135 from that sky-high Con Ed bill, but few people are applying
item.description: Many New York city utility customers are dealing with increased rates and high electric or gas usage after the winter storm. The company says nearly 600,000 people could be eligible, but only hundreds have applied since a state program expanded last month. [ more › ]

item.title: NYC parents say Mount Sinai has cut off services for trans kids ahead of federal rule
item.description: Parents and advocates say Mount Sinai has stopped providing gender-affirming care. Mount Sinai would be the second major NYC health system to end services for trans youth amid threats from the Trump administration. [ more › ]

item.title: NYC nurses strike ends after NewYork-Presbyterian nurses ratify new contract
item.description: Nurses at NewYork-Presbyterian overwhelmingly voted to ratify a new three-year contract on Saturday, ending the 41-day strike. [ more › ]

item.title: Environmental groups sue NYC over Willets Point wastewater plant
item.description: The banks of Flushing Creek, near where the city plans to build a water treatment plant. Local leaders have also raised concerns that a new plant could threaten aquatic life. [ more › ]

item.title: New York City could see up to 2 feet of snow through Monday, NWS warns
item.description: People cross the street during the winter storm in New York City on Sunday, January 25, 2026. The mayor is expected to make a decision on moving Monday’s public school classes to remote learning by noon Sunday. [ more › ]

item.title: Here’s what’s been cancelled in New York and New Jersey due to the coming blizzard
item.description: A Coca-Cola polar bear takes a drink from his bottle in an ad at the snow-bound entrance to the subway on Broadway and 22nd Street in 2003. Transit agencies have already planned modified schedules for Monday, and warn that further cancellations could come later. [ more › ]

item.title: New York lawmakers seek rent control to protect small businesses
item.description: Marlow & Sons ended its 21-year run in Williamsburg last year following a rent increase. A new bill would regulate rents and leases for bodegas, restaurants, and mom-and-pop shops. [ more › ]

item.title: Mamdani announces snow day, NYC schools fully closed Monday
item.description: People go sledding in the snow at Cedar Hill in Central Park in New York City on January 25, 2026. The mayor said it will be New York City’s first old school snow day since 2019. [ more › ]

item.title: Travel ban starting Sunday evening on NYC roads due to blizzard
item.description: The worst of the blizzard is expected to begin at 6 p.m. Mayor Zohran Mamdani ordered the ban, which lasts until noon Monday. [ more › ]

item.title: Winter of NYC discontent: Bummer blizzard comes just as filthy snow was melting away
item.description: A miserable scene. Times Square in a blizzard. New Yorkers sought solace in the drink as the blizzard bore down. [ more › ]
